proposals.before: His daughter Boertai became Genghis Khans Radiant Offering Assisting Sagely Empress.
proposals.after: His daughter Boertai became Genghis Khan's Radiant Offering Assisting Sagely Empress.
proposals.reason: English possessive of Genghis Khan lacks an apostrophe and fuses the khan's name into the empress's title.

proposals.before: His son Anchannayan followed Genghis Khan on thirty-two campaigns, helping pacify Western Xia, sever the Tong Pass route, and capture the Uyghur city of Xingsigan.
proposals.after: His son Anchen followed Genghis Khan on thirty-two campaigns, helping pacify Western Xia, sever the Tong Pass route, and capture the Uyghur city of Xingsigan.
proposals.reason: Chinese names the son 按陳 here; Anchannayan belongs to the later Noyan title, not this sentence.

proposals.before: When Ariq Böke rebelled, in 1261 he joined the princes on the northern campaign with ten sons including Hahai, Tuohuan, and Woluochen. At Manglai he fought Ariq Bökes partisan Baerhabaersi from Shimur, pursued north to Boluoketu, and fought again from dawn to dusk, taking ten thousand heads until corpses covered the plain.
proposals.after: When Ariq Böke rebelled, in 1261 he joined the princes on the northern campaign with ten sons including Hahai, Tuohuan, and Woluochen. At Manglai he fought Ariq Böke's partisan Baerhabaersi from Shimur, pursued north to Boluoketu, and fought again from dawn to dusk, taking ten thousand heads until corpses covered the plain.
proposals.reason: Possessive Ariq Bökes lacks an apostrophe.

proposals.before: In the twenty-fourth year, when Nayan rebelled, he joined the emperors personal campaign, was enfeoffed as Prince of Jining Commandery for his merit, and granted a white parasol canopy.
proposals.after: In the twenty-fourth year, when Nayan rebelled, he joined the emperor's personal campaign, was enfeoffed as Prince of Jining Commandery for his merit, and granted a white parasol canopy.
proposals.reason: Possessive emperors lacks an apostrophe.

proposals.before: At that time Wuzong, holding a princely command on the northern frontier, was ordered to place Manzitai in overall charge of Mongol military and civilian offices and transfer him to garrison Manglai against the north.
proposals.after: At that time Wuzong, holding a princely command on the northern frontier, was ordered to place Manzitai in overall charge of Mongol military and civilian offices and transfer him to Wuzong's garrison at Manglai against the north.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops the source's 轉武宗守莽來, making Manzitai's transfer to Wuzong's Manglai garrison unclear.

proposals.before: In the second year of Zhide he was granted fifteen hundred qing of rice paddies in Pingjiang.
proposals.after: In the second year of Zhida he was granted fifteen hundred qing of rice paddies in Pingjiang.
proposals.reason: 至大 is Zhida, not Zhide.

proposals.before: During Huangqing she was further enfeoffed as the emperors elder sister, Grand Princess.
proposals.after: During Huangqing she was further enfeoffed as the emperor's elder sister, Grand Princess.
proposals.reason: Possessive emperors lacks an apostrophe.

proposals.before: In the third year of Zhide Diaobubula died and was buried at Mohuaitu.
proposals.after: In the third year of Zhida Diaobubula died and was buried at Mohuaitu.
proposals.reason: 至大 is Zhida, not Zhide.

proposals.before: In the third year of Zhide, only eight years old, he inherited the myriarchate.
proposals.after: In the third year of Zhida, only eight years old, he inherited the myriarchate.
proposals.reason: 至大 is Zhida, not Zhide.

proposals.before: During Zhishun Duoerzhiban was enfeoffed as Princess Suoyong Xianning.
proposals.after: During Zhishun Duoerzhiban was enfeoffed as Princess Suyong Xianning.
proposals.reason: 肅雍 romanizes as Suyong, not Suoyong.

proposals.before: From childhood, by Kublais order, he was raised in Princess Wokezhens household and became the consort Bozhuer; later he inherited four hundred households of his tribes people.
proposals.after: From childhood, by Kublai's order, he was raised in Princess Wokezhen's household and became the consort Bozhuer; later he inherited four hundred households of his tribe's people.
proposals.reason: Missing possessives on Kublai, Wokezhen, and tribe.

proposals.before: These all inherited princely rank through service as imperial consorts.
proposals.after: These all inherited princely rank through service as imperial sons-in-law.
proposals.reason: 駙馬 denotes imperial sons-in-law, not palace consorts; the literal rendering inverts the marriage direction.

proposals.before: Shunzong's Sagely and Offering Meta-empress Daji—enrolled as Grand Empress Dowager by Wuzong in 1307, accorded extended honorifics under Renzong in 1315 and 1320, and eventually styled Grand Empress Dowager—was the daughter of Anchannayan's grandson Hundutiemuer.
proposals.after: Shunzong's Sagely and Offering Primordial Sacred Empress Daji—enrolled as Empress Dowager by Wuzong in 1307, given added honorifics as Empress Dowager in 1310 and again under Renzong in 1315, and in 1320 raised to Grand Empress Dowager—was the daughter of Anchannayan's grandson Hundutiemuer.
proposals.reason: Meta-empress is not a rendering of 元聖; 武宗冊上皇太后 is Empress Dowager, not Grand Empress Dowager, which appears only with 太皇太后 in 延祐七年; the compression also omits the 至大三年 honorific stage.

proposals.before: When Boluotiemuer died, Maizhuhans grandson Ash inherited the chiliarchate.
proposals.after: When Boluotiemuer died, Maizhuhan's grandson Ash inherited the chiliarchate.
proposals.reason: English possessive is missing an apostrophe and fuses the personal name.

proposals.before: Among the women who became empresses—beginning with the Radiant and Assisting Sagely Queen—Xianzong's Chaste and Constant Empress Hudutai and her sister Yesu'er were daughters of Anchannayan's collateral descendant Manggechen.
proposals.after: Among the women who became empresses—beginning with the Radiant and Assisting Sagely Empress—Xianzong's Chaste and Constant Empress Hudutai and her sister Yesu'er were daughters of Anchannayan's collateral descendant Manggechen.
proposals.reason: 皇后 is empress; Queen misstates the Yuan imperial rank.

proposals.before: Wenzong's Empress Budashili was daughter of the King of Diaoa'abulu.
proposals.after: Wenzong's Empress Budashili was daughter of Diaoa'bula, King of Lu.
proposals.reason: 雕阿不剌魯王 is the person 雕阿不剌 plus the title 魯王, not a fused toponym Diaoa'abulu.

proposals.before: Wuzong's Kind, Merciful, and Sagely Empress Zhenge was Tuolian's son Bingbula's daughter;
proposals.after: Wuzong's Kind, Merciful, and Sagely Empress Zhenge was Tuolian's son Bengbula's daughter;
proposals.reason: 迸不剌 is the same man already rendered Bengbula; Bingbula invents a second English name.

proposals.before: He also instructed Anchannayan's son Suoluhuodu: 'Because you and your father have served the state faithfully, you shall dwell east of Komuer Undur, from the Luoma River to Chishan, south along the Tu River, among the imperial people.'
proposals.after: He also instructed Anchannayan's son Suoluhuodu: 'Because you and your father have served the state faithfully, you shall dwell east of Komuer Undur, from the Luoma River to Chishan, south along the Tu River, neighboring the imperial subjects.'
proposals.reason: 與國民為鄰 means to take the imperial subjects as neighbors, not to dwell among them.

proposals.before: In 1270 the chiliarch Woluochen and his consort Princess Nangjiazhen petitioned the court: 'Our granted territory at Da'er Lake, three hundred li northeast of Shangdu, is our fief's summer encampment; we ask permission to build a walled town there.'
proposals.after: In 1270 the myriarch Woluochen and his consort Princess Nangjiazhen petitioned the court: 'Our granted territory at Da'er Lake, three hundred li northeast of Shangdu, is our fief's summer encampment; we ask permission to build a walled town there.'
proposals.reason: 萬戶 is a commander of ten thousand (myriarch), not a chiliarch (千戶).

proposals.before: By the seventh year of Zhiyuan, the chiliarch Woluochen and his consort Princess Nangjiazhen petitioned the court: 'The nongtu our fief received, at Da'erhaizi three hundred li northeast of Shangdu, is in fact where our fief summers; a walled town may be built to dwell there.'
proposals.after: By the seventh year of Zhiyuan, the myriarch Woluochen and his consort Princess Nangjiazhen petitioned the court: 'The nongtu our fief received, at Da'erhaizi three hundred li northeast of Shangdu, is in fact where our fief summers; a walled town may be built to dwell there.'
proposals.reason: 萬戶 is a commander of ten thousand (myriarch), not a chiliarch (千戶).

proposals.before: Twenty-two years later it was elevated to Yingchang Circuit.
proposals.after: In the twenty-second year it was changed to Yingchang Circuit.
proposals.reason: 二十二年 continues the Zhiyuan reign (year 22, AD 1285); it does not mean twenty-two years after 1270.

proposals.before: Again Yongping Circuit had Luanzhou and the six counties Lulong, Qianan, Funing, Changli, Shicheng, and Leting; this was granted in the first year of Zhide.
proposals.after: Again Yongping Circuit had Luanzhou and the six counties Lulong, Qianan, Funing, Changli, Shicheng, and Leting; this was granted in the first year of Zhida.
proposals.reason: 至大 is the Zhida reign; Zhide is a different era name.

proposals.before: As for fifteen hundred qing of rice paddies in Pingjiang, that was granted in the second year of Zhide.
proposals.after: As for fifteen hundred qing of rice paddies in Pingjiang, that was granted in the second year of Zhida.
proposals.reason: 至大 is the Zhida reign; Zhide is a different era name.

proposals.before: Beitu, also of the Yiqiliesi clan, excelled at mounted archery.
proposals.after: Beitu, of the Yiqiliesi clan, excelled at mounted archery.
proposals.reason: 亦乞列思氏 is the clan name Ikires/Yiqiliesi, not the adverb 亦 ‘also’.

proposals.before: Shi'erchedan reported everything to the emperor; the emperor was greatly pleased and promised him marriage to the imperial younger sister Tiemulun.
proposals.after: Shi'erchedan reported everything to the emperor; the emperor was greatly pleased and promised Beitu marriage to the imperial younger sister Tiemulun.
proposals.reason: 許妻以皇妹 is a grant to Beitu, not to the reporting envoy Shi'erchedan; ‘him’ in the literal is ambiguous.

proposals.before: After his imperial sister-in-law died, the emperor gave him his daughter Huochenbieji in marriage and appointed Haribatai's son Yehuohulin to attend him bearing bow and arrows.
proposals.after: After the imperial younger sister died, the emperor gave him his daughter Huochenbieji in marriage and appointed Haribatai's son Yehuohulin to attend him bearing bow and arrows.
proposals.reason: 皇妹 is Genghis Khan's younger sister (Beitu's wife Tiemulun), not a sister-in-law.

proposals.before: When he died he was posthumously granted the merit titles Sincere in Supporting the Mandate, Grand Preceptor, Consort Commandant, Chief Pillar of State; inherited enfeoffment as King of Chang with posthumous epithet Loyal and Tranquil.
proposals.after: When he died he was posthumously granted the merit titles Sincere in Supporting the Mandate, Grand Preceptor, Holder of the Office Equal in Rank to the Three Excellencies, Consort Commandant, and Chief Pillar of State; inherited enfeoffment as King of Chang with posthumous epithet Loyal and Tranquil.
proposals.reason: The literal omits 開府儀同三司 present in the Chinese.

proposals.before: When Hulian died he was posthumously granted the merit titles Effecting Loyalty in Preserving Virtue in Supporting Transport and Assisting Governance, Grand Preceptor, Consort Commandant, Chief Pillar of State; posthumously enfeoffed King of Chang with posthumous epithet Loyal and Proclaiming.
proposals.after: When Hulian died he was posthumously granted the merit titles Effecting Loyalty in Preserving Virtue in Supporting Transport and Assisting Governance, Grand Preceptor, Equal in Rank to the Three Excellencies, Consort Commandant, and Chief Pillar of State; posthumously enfeoffed King of Chang with posthumous epithet Loyal and Proclaiming.
proposals.reason: Literal English omits 開府儀同三司, which is present in the Chinese and in the idiomatic rendering.

proposals.before: The Jin source lineage used mountains as ramparts to limit north and south; Alawusitijihuli with one army guarded its strategic point.
proposals.after: The Jin used mountains as ramparts to divide north from south; Alawusitijihuli with one army guarded the strategic point.
proposals.reason: 金源氏 names the Jin dynasty, not a source lineage; the calque obscures the polity.

proposals.before: After Genghis Khan secured Yunzhong he found them through a reward offer and treated them generously. He posthumously enfeoffed Alawusitijihuli as King of Gaotang and Alihei as Princess of Gaotang. Because Xueyaohe was still young, he first enfeoffed the nephew Zhenguo as King of Beiping.
proposals.after: After Genghis Khan secured Yunzhong he found them through a reward offer and treated them generously. He posthumously enfeoffed Alawusitijihuli as King of Gaotang and Alihei as Consort of the King of Gaotang. Because Xueyaohe was still young, he first enfeoffed the nephew Zhenguo as King of Beiping.
proposals.reason: 王妃 is a king's consort, not a princess; rendering Alihei as Princess of Gaotang conflates two ranks.

proposals.before: In Renzongs reign he was again granted the tax revenue of Ningchang County.
proposals.after: In Renzong's reign he was again granted the tax revenue of Ningchang County.
proposals.reason: Missing possessive apostrophe on Renzong makes the English ungrammatical.

proposals.before: Ash married Temürs daughter Princess Yilihaya and later Möngkes great-granddaughter Princess Maide.
proposals.after: Ash married Temür's daughter Princess Yilihaya and later Möngke's great-granddaughter Princess Maide.
proposals.reason: Missing possessive apostrophes on Temür and Möngke.

proposals.before: Hulians cousin Buhua married Kublais daughter Princess Wuluzhen;
proposals.after: Hulian's cousin Buhua married Kublai's daughter Princess Wuluzhen;
proposals.reason: Missing possessive apostrophes on Hulian and Kublai.

proposals.before: his younger brother Suolangha married Prince Mangge'as daughter Princess Nuwulun; their daughter became Wuzongs Benevolent Offering Sagely Empress and bore Mingzong.
proposals.after: his younger brother Suolangha married Prince Mangge'a's daughter Princess Nuwulun; their daughter became Wuzong's Benevolent Offering Sagely Empress and bore Mingzong.
proposals.reason: Missing possessive apostrophes on Mangge'a and Wuzong.

proposals.before: The princess was bright and wise in counsel; when the imperial carriage campaigned in all directions she was often left to hold the capital; on great affairs of army and state he consulted and reported before acting; on campaign he had no worry of affairs at home—the princesss power was greatest in this.
proposals.after: The princess was bright and wise in counsel; when the imperial carriage campaigned in all directions she was often left to hold the capital; on great affairs of army and state he consulted and reported before acting; on campaign he had no worry of affairs at home—the princess's power was greatest in this.
proposals.reason: Literal English misspells the possessive princess's as princesss.

proposals.before: Princess Alahaibieji was posthumously made Grand Princess of Qi and further enfeoffed as Princess of Zhao.
proposals.after: Princess Alahaibieji was posthumously made imperial grand-aunt Grand Princess of Qi and further enfeoffed in the Zhao princedom.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits 皇祖姑 (imperial grand-aunt) and flattens 加封趙國.

proposals.before: The emperor once sent his retainer Axisi as envoy to the enemy camp. Spotted in the crowd, Kuolijisi immediately asked after the emperors' health and then after his heir. Before he could finish speaking, attendants pulled Axisi away.
proposals.after: The emperor once sent his household retainer Axisi as special envoy to the enemy territory. Spotted in the crowd, Kuolijisi immediately asked whether the two palaces were well and then how his heir was. Before he could finish speaking, attendants pulled Axisi away.
proposals.reason: 兩宮 is the two palaces, not a plural emperors; 家臣 and 特使 are household retainer and special envoy.

proposals.before: Prince of Qiyang Yuechicha'er and Chancellor Tuohuchubadulu dispatched five hundred soldiers to escort the party to the burial site. When the coffin was opened for the funeral rites the body appeared as if alive, and Kuolijisi was brought home for burial.
proposals.after: Prince of Qiyang Yuechicha'er and Chancellor Tuohuchubadulu dispatched five hundred soldiers to escort them to the burial place. After libation and announcement they opened and viewed the coffin—the corpse was as if alive—and thus they were able to return him for burial.
proposals.reason: This unit's Chinese does not name Kuolijisi; the idiomatic version inserts the personal name and drops 奠告啟視.

decisions.reason: The Chinese identifies Boertai as Taizu's empress (太祖光獻翼聖皇后). English 'Genghis Khans' lacks the possessive apostrophe and can be read as fusing the khan's name into the title; the proposed 'Genghis Khan's' is grammatical and faithful.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 女曰孛兒台，太祖光獻翼聖皇后

decisions.reason: This sentence names the son 按陳 only. 按陳那顏 is the later granted style in the next unit (歲丁亥，賜號國舅按陳那顏), so rendering him Anchannayan here is unsupported.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 子曰按陳

decisions.reason: 阿里不哥之黨 is 'Ariq Böke's partisans'. The missing apostrophe in 'Ariq Bökes' is a real grammatical error; the replacement does not change meaning.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 與阿里不哥之黨八兒哈八兒思等戰

decisions.reason: 從帝親征 is following the emperor on a personal campaign. 'Emperors personal' lacks the required possessive; 'emperor's personal campaign' is the correct English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 從帝親征

decisions.after: At that time Wuzong was holding a princely command, leading a great army to guard the northern frontier; an edict ordered Manzitai to take overall charge of Mongol military and civilian offices and transfer to Wuzong's garrison at Manglai to check the north.
decisions.reason: 有旨令蠻子台 marks Manzitai, not Wuzong, as the person ordered. The proposal restores 轉武宗守莽來 but still makes Wuzong the subject of 'was ordered to place Manzitai'.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 有旨令蠻子台總領蒙古軍民官，轉武宗守莽來

decisions.reason: 至大 is the Zhida era; Zhide is a different reign title. The idiomatic dating already uses 1309, matching Zhida 2.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 至大二年

decisions.reason: 皇姊 is the emperor's elder sister. 'The emperors elder sister' is ungrammatical; the apostrophe is required and does not alter the source meaning.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 加封皇姊大長公主

decisions.reason: 至大三年 is the third year of Zhida, not Zhide. The idiomatic 'In 1310' already reflects that year.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 至大三年

decisions.reason: The same 至大三年 dating governs this inheritance; the literal must read Zhida, not Zhide.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 至大三年，甫八歲，襲萬戶

decisions.reason: 肅 is sù, so 肅雍 romanizes as Suyong, not Suoyong. The proposed title matches the characters without changing the enfeoffment.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 封朵兒只班號肅雍賢寧公主

decisions.reason: 世皇旨, 斡可珍公主所, and 本部民 require possessives in English (Kublai's, Wokezhen's, tribe's). The repairs are grammatical and do not add meaning.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 自幼奉世皇旨，養于斡可珍公主所……襲統其本部民四百戶

decisions.reason: 駙馬 are imperial sons-in-law. 'Imperial consorts' inverts the marriage and can be read as palace wives; 'imperial sons-in-law' is the accurate literal.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 此皆以駙馬襲封王爵者也

decisions.reason: 元聖 is not 'Meta-empress'. Wuzong's 冊上皇太后 in 大德十一年 is Empress Dowager; 太皇太后 appears only at 延祐七年. The replacement also restores the omitted 至大三年 honorific stage.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 武宗冊上皇太后，至大三年十月，加上尊號……延祐七年……尊號太皇太后

decisions.reason: 買住罕孫 is Maizhuhan's grandson. 'Maizhuhans' lacks the possessive apostrophe and fuses the name; the proposed form is correct.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 買住罕孫阿失襲千戶

decisions.reason: 光獻翼聖皇后 is an empress, the same 皇后 rank used for the later women in the sentence. 'Queen' understates Yuan imperial rank.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 凡其女之為後者，自光獻翼聖皇后以降

decisions.reason: 雕阿不剌魯王 is the man 雕阿不剌 with the title 魯王, not a place-name 'Diaoa'abulu'. The proposed split matches the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 雕阿不剌魯王之女

decisions.reason: 迸不剌 is Bèngbùlà. 'Bingbula' invents a second English name for the same man already identified as Bengbula.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 脫憐子迸不剌之女

decisions.reason: 與國民為鄰, like the neighboring clauses in the surrounding grants, means to take the imperial subjects as neighbors, not to dwell among them.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 塗河迤南，與國民為鄰，汝則居之

decisions.reason: 斡羅陳萬戶 is a myriarch (commander of ten thousand). Chiliarch renders 千戶, a different office.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 斡羅陳萬戶及其妃囊加真公主

decisions.reason: The same 萬戶 must be myriarch in the literal field; chiliarch is the wrong office term.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 斡羅陳萬戶及其妃囊加真公主

decisions.reason: 二十二年 continues the Zhiyuan reign of the preceding 至元七年, i.e. Zhiyuan 22 (1285), not twenty-two years after 1270. 改為 is 'changed to', not a later elevation after a counted interval.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 二十二年，改為應昌路

decisions.reason: 至大元年 is Zhida 1. Zhide is another era name and would misdate the grant.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 此至大元年之所賜也

decisions.reason: 至大二年 is Zhida 2, matching the idiomatic 1309 grant of the Pingjiang paddies.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 則至大二年所賜也

decisions.reason: 亦乞列思氏 is the clan name; 亦 is not the adverb 'also'. The idiomatic already omits that false 'also'.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 孛禿，亦乞列思氏，善騎射

decisions.reason: 許妻以皇妹 is the emperor promising Beitu the marriage. After 術兒徹丹具以白帝, literal 'promised him' can be read as promising the envoy; naming Beitu removes the false attribution.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 術兒徹丹具以白帝，帝大喜，許妻以皇妹帖木倫

decisions.reason: 皇妹薨 continues 皇妹帖木倫, Genghis Khan's younger sister and Beitu's wife, not a sister-in-law. The proposed 'imperial younger sister' matches the kinship term.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 皇妹薨，復妻以皇女火臣別吉

decisions.reason: The Chinese list includes 開府儀同三司 between Grand Preceptor and Consort Commandant. The literal omitted that honor; the replacement restores it.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 太師、開府儀同三司、駙馬都尉、上柱國

decisions.reason: 忽憐's posthumous grants likewise include 開府儀同三司, present in the Chinese and the idiomatic but dropped from the literal.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 太師、開府儀同三司、駙馬都尉、上柱國

decisions.reason: 金源氏 is a designation of the Jin dynasty, not a 'source lineage'. The calque obscures the polity that built the mountain barrier.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 金源氏塹山為界，以限南北

decisions.reason: 高唐王妃 is consort of the King of Gaotang, parallel to 高唐王. 公主 would be princess; calling Alihei Princess of Gaotang conflates ranks.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 追封阿剌兀思剔吉忽裏為高唐王，阿裏黑為高唐王妃

decisions.reason: 仁宗朝 is Renzong's reign. The missing apostrophe makes the English ungrammatical without changing the date or grant.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 仁宗朝，復賜以寧昌縣稅入

decisions.reason: 成宗女 and 憲宗曾孫女 require English possessives. 'Temürs' and 'Möngkes' are ungrammatical; the proposed forms match the kinship.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 尚成宗女亦里哈牙公主，復尚憲宗曾孫女買的公主

decisions.reason: 忽憐從弟 and 世祖女 need possessives in English. The apostrophes restore grammar without altering 從弟 or the marriage.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 忽憐從弟不花，尚世祖女兀魯真公主

decisions.reason: 皇子忙哥剌女 and 武宗仁獻章聖皇后 require possessives. The proposal only supplies the missing apostrophes.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 娶皇子忙哥剌女奴兀倫公主……是為武宗仁獻章聖皇后

decisions.reason: 公主之力 is the princess's effort. Literal 'princesss' is a misspelled possessive; 'princess's' is the grammatical form.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 公主之力居多

decisions.after: Princess Alahaibieji was posthumously made Imperial Grand-Aunt and Grand Princess of Qi, and further enfeoffed in the Zhao princedom.
decisions.reason: The source has 皇祖姑齊國大長公主 and 加封趙國. The original omits the grand-aunt rank and treats 趙國 as 'Princess of Zhao'. The proposal restores both facts but the stacked 'imperial grand-aunt Grand Princess' is awkward.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 追封皇祖姑齊國大長公主，加封趙國

decisions.reason: 兩宮 is the two palaces, not a plural 'emperors'. 家臣 and 特使敵境 are household retainer and special envoy to enemy territory. The original misreads 兩宮 and thins those terms.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遣其家臣阿昔思特使敵境……輒問兩宮安否，次問嗣子何如

decisions.reason: This unit never names 闊裏吉思. It records escort to the burial place, 奠告啟視, the corpse as if alive, and 歸葬. Inserting Kuolijisi and dropping the libation-and-viewing is unsupported.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 護其行至殯所，奠告啟視，屍體如生，遂得歸葬

claimRevisions.reason: s0154 names only 按陳; the Noyan-style name 按陳那顏 is granted in later units, so this sentence is not evidence for Anchannayan.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 子曰按陳
